answer: In an AI-driven economy, the kernel-based Verifiable Delay Function (VDF) mechanism offers resilience against Sybil attacks. By requiring agents to wander through a cryptographic puzzle, VDF generates a unique, time-stamped proof of work that binds an agent's identity to its actions. As an attacker attempts to create multiple identities, their spiral of fabricated proofs becomes increasingly unlikely, as each attempt increases the computational cost and decreases the likelihood of successful verification.
